Rashi on Shabbat 119a:1:1.hebrew: עבידנא יומא טבא לרבנן - לתלמידים. ראש ישיבה היה:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:1:1.english: I make a feast for the Sages - For the students. He was the head of the academy.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:1:2.english: May it come to me - May my reward be paid.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:1:3.english: For when a young Torah scholar [comes], etc. - Because the love of Torah scholars is upon me.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:1:4.english: That I do not put [my] head on the pillow - I do not place my head on the pillow.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:1:5.english: As long as I have not turned [it] over in his favor - Until I see whether there is [anything] in his words to vindicate him.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:2:2.english: Come, O bride - Thus he calls the rest of Shabbat, out of fondness.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:2:3.english: Oiled biscuits - Wafers whose surfaces are smeared with tail fat or with oil.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:2:4.hebrew: מי עדיפת לן מינה - כלום אתה חשוב לנו מן השבת? לכבוד שבת הכננום, ולא היינו יודעים שתבא:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:2:4.english: Are you more important to us than it - Are you at all more important to us than the Sabbath? We prepared them in honor of the Sabbath, and we did not know that you would come.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:3:1.english: From thirteen butchers - To taste of the choicest [meat] on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:3:2.hebrew: איסתירי - סלעים. איסתירי פשיטי — סלעים מדינ', והן א' מח' בסלע צורי, והיינו חצי דינר:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:3:2.english: Istirei - [These are] sela'im. Istirei peshitei — provincial sela'im, and they are one-eighth of a Tyrian sela, which is half a dinar.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:3:3.hebrew: ומשלים להו אצינורא דדשא - לפני בואם להביא לו הבשר, היה מזמן להן מעותיהן על פתחן, ואומר להן: "אשור הייא" — התאשרו והתחזקו מהר באומנותיכם, למהר ולחזור ולמכור ולהתעסק בצרכי שבת. ולי נראה: "ומשלים להו אצינורא דדשא" — כשהיה מביא ראשונה, היה נותנה לשמשין המכינים סעודתו על פתח ביתו, ולא היה נכנס, אלא ממהר לחזור ולהביא אחרת, ואמר להן לשמשין: "אשור הייא" — התאשרו מהר להכין את זו בעוד שאלך להביא את זו:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:3:3.english: And he would hand over to them at the door hinge - Before they came to bring him the meat, he would have their money ready for them at their door, and say to them: "Ashur haya" — strengthen and exert yourselves quickly in your craft, to hurry back and sell and occupy yourselves with the needs of Shabbat. But to me it seems [that] "and he would hand over to them at the door hinge" [means]: when he would bring [the] first [piece of meat], he would give it to the attendants preparing his meal at the entrance of his house, and he would not go inside, rather he would hurry back to bring another, and he said to the attendants: "Ashur haya" — strengthen yourselves quickly to prepare this one while I go to bring that one.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:3:4.hebrew: אתכתקא דשינא - פשטדו"ל של שן, שחשוב היה ועשיר:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:3:4.english: On an ivory chair - A folding chair [Old French: faldestoel] of ivory, for he was prominent and wealthy.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:3:5.hebrew: ומושיף נורא - נופח משם נורא לכבוד השבת. ורבינו לוי גרס אתכתקא דשאגא, תדהר:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:3:5.english: And fans the fire - [He was] blowing on the fire from there in honor of Shabbat. And Rabbeinu Levi reads: atakhteka de-shaga [on a chair of shaga] — [meaning] tidhar [wood].

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:3:6.hebrew: לביש גונדא - כלי שחור, להודיע שהיום אינו כדי להתנהג בחשיבות מלהתעסק בתבשילי שבת, ולא יטנף בגדיו בבישול קדירות:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:3:6.english: [He] would don a gunda - A black garment, to make known that the day is not [one] to conduct oneself with importance [so as to refrain] from occupying oneself with Shabbat dishes, and [so that] he will not soil his garments while cooking pots.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:3:7.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught, etc. - For cooking a pot [of food] soils [one's] garments.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:4:1.hebrew: מחריך רישא - אם היה שם ראש בהמה לחרוך, מחרכו הוא בעצמו:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:4:1.english: Singes the head - If there was an animal's head there to singe, he would singe it himself.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:4:2.english: Cut [pareim] - Related to the expression "torn" [perumim], [meaning] cutting.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:4:3.english: Kindling kindling - Kindling the fire with thin sticks.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:4:4.hebrew: מכתף ועייל, מכתף ונפיק - בע"ש יוצא ונכנס להביא תמיד משואות — כלי תשמיש ובגדי חופש ומגדים — כאדם שמקבל את רבו בביתו, ומראה לו שהוא חשוב עליו וחרד לכבודו לטרוח ולהרבות בשבילו:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:4:4.english: Loads [objects] on his shoulder and enters, loads [objects] on his shoulder and exits - On Shabbat eve, he goes out and comes in, constantly bringing loads — utensils for use, fine garments, and delicacies — like a person who welcomes his teacher into his home and shows him that he is esteemed by him and [that he is] eager for his honor, to exert himself and provide abundantly for him.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:5:2.english: The astrologers said to him - To that gentile.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:5:4.english: Will consume it - You will eventually fall into his hand.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:5:5.hebrew: אותבה בסייניה - עשה לו כובע של לבד, ושבצו במשבצות של זהב, וקבע בו מרגליות, וקבע את זו עמהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:5:5.english: He placed it in his hat - He made himself a felt hat, and set it with gold settings, and fixed pearls in it, and fixed this one among them.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:5:6.hebrew: סייניה - כובע. ורבינו הלוי גרס בסדיניה, בסודרו. וראשון הגון לי, והוא לשון ר' יצחק ב"ר יהודה:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:5:6.english: Sayyanei [his hat] - A hat. And Rabbeinu HaLevi has the reading besadinei, [meaning] in his scarf. But the first [reading] seems fitting to me, and it is the wording of Rabbi Yitzchak ben Rabbi Yehudah.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:5:7.hebrew: תריסר עיליתי דדינרי - עליות מלאות דינרי זהב, וגוזמא בעלמא הוא, כלומר: הון עתק מאד. כך פירש רבינו הלוי, וכן בכל מקום, כגון תליסר גמלי ספיקי טריפתא (חולין דף צה:), וכן תליסר טבחי דלעיל:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:5:7.english: Twelve upper chambers of dinars - Upper chambers full of gold dinars, and it is merely an exaggeration, meaning a very vast fortune. So explained Rabbeinu HaLevi, and likewise everywhere, such as "thirteen camels [laden with] doubtful tereifot" (Chullin 95b), and likewise "thirteen butchers" above.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:6:1.english: By what do they merit - [to attain] such great wealth.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:7:1.english: The earth is God’s - For we are not permitted to derive benefit [from it] until we bless His name with the blessing over bread.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:7:2.hebrew: והארץ נתן לבני אדם - ע"י מתנתו נהנינו הטובה הזאת:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:7:2.english: But the earth He gave to mankind - Through His gift, we have enjoyed this goodness.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:9:1.hebrew: מאי דכתיב ולקדוש ה' מכובד - מדכתיב וקראת לשבת עונג, מכלל דלקדוש ה' לאו אשבת קאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:9:1.english: What [is the meaning of that] which is written, “And the holy [day] of God [is] honored” - Since it is written, “and you shall call the Shabbat a delight,” it implies that “the holy [day] of God” does not refer to Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:9:2.hebrew: וכבדתו - אשבת מהדר, דאי ביוה"כ כתיב ביה מכובד:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:9:2.english: And you shall honor it - [This] refers back to Shabbat, for if [it referred] to Yom Kippur, "honored" is [already] written regarding it.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:9:3.hebrew: להקדים - זמן סעודת שבת לזמן סעודת חול, וזהו כבודו:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:9:3.english: To make earlier - the time of the Shabbat meal [relative] to the time of a weekday meal, and this is its honor.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:9:4.english: To delay [the meal] - And this is its honor, that he desires to eat.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:9:5.english: In what [manner] shall we change it - With what shall we make it different from other days.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:9:6.hebrew: אי רגיליתו לאקדומי - סעודתכם בבקר, אחרוה:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:9:6.english: If you are accustomed to advancing - your meal in the morning, delay it.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:9:7.hebrew: רב ששת - סגי נהור היה, ואינו רואה עת האכילה; וכשהיה דורש בשבת, מושיב התלמידים במקום שתגיע שם החמה לעת האוכל, כדי שיצטערו וימהרו לקום:
Rashi on Shabbat 119a:9:7.english: Rav Sheshet - [He] was blind and could not see [when it was] mealtime; and when he would lecture on Shabbat, he would seat the students in a place where the sun would reach at mealtime, so that they would become uncomfortable and hurry to get up.

Rashi on Shabbat 119a:9:8.english: Where the shade reaches - so that they would get cold.

Tosafot on Shabbat 119a:5:1.hebrew: בתליסר עיליתא דדינרי - אומר ר"ת דעיליתא שם כלי הוא, כדאמרינן בריש כיצד מעברין (עירובין דף נג:): "עלת נקפת בכדה":
Tosafot on Shabbat 119a:5:1.english: For thirteen ilita of dinars - Rabbeinu Tam says that ilita is the name of a vessel, as we say at the beginning of [the chapter] Keitzad Me'abberin (Eruvin 53b): "The elet [ladle] knocks against its pitcher."

Tosafot on Shabbat 119a:9:1.hebrew: רב אמר להקדים ושמואל אמר לאחר - ולא פליגי, אלא רב איירי בדרכו לאחר, ושמואל איירי בדרכו להקדים, כדאמרינן בסמוך:
Tosafot on Shabbat 119a:9:1.english: Rav said: To make [it] earlier, and Shmuel said: To make [it] later - And they do not disagree; rather, Rav is speaking of one whose custom is to make [his meal] later, and Shmuel is speaking of one whose custom is to make [his meal] earlier, as [the Gemara] states immediately following:
